decisions.reason: The same message separately changes source selection to one YouTube video, which is already represented by the candidate's message-84 MODIFY; the visual editing style change does not further alter source-selection state.
Moment completeness and educational value are independently established by separate clauses in the message and are not changed by the polished, straightforward visual editing requirement.
Avoiding excessive effects and using polished editing does not necessarily change the existing requirement to use color in captions.
The visual editing style decision does not alter the existing 30–90-second duration limits.
Message 84 governs the later requalification clips and does not retroactively change the independently defined initial trial batch.
The polished visual editing and effects policy does not modify the independently defined effective-hook requirement.
The source concerns a distinct three-clip requalification batch and does not necessarily revise the earlier 15–20-clip extended trial batch.

The visual editing standard applies to the requalification clips but does not change the batch's count or approval-based acceptance condition; the detailed editing behavior remains owned by the atomic visual-editing Requirement.
Message 84 repeats the existing target of 125 approved clips per month, while the visual editing style change does not alter that quota.
